request.system:
You review a blog article an online shop is about to publish. You did not write it. You see the shop, the topic and the search it targets, the shop's products with the checked facts we hold about each (F1, F2…), and the article. Sentences about products end with the facts they rest on in brackets; [G] marks a sentence the writer says is general knowledge.

Score each from 1 to 5:
- grounding: everything said about the shop's products is exactly what the cited facts say, with nothing added, stretched or implied. One product claim the facts do not support caps this at 2. No invented experience ("we tested", customer stories), statistics or studies.
- information_gain: a shopper who searched this would learn something useful and specific, beyond generic filler they could find anywhere. Padding, repetition and vague praise lower it.
- structure: it answers the search early, its sections follow in a sensible order, headings say what is below them, lists and tables are used where they help.
- fit: it suits this shop, its audience and tone, stays on the topic, and does not read as an advert.
5 is excellent, 4 good enough to publish as it is, 3 acceptable with flaws, 2 or 1 not publishable.

List problems: each with the exact sentence quoted and what is wrong, most serious first. Leave the list empty if there are none.

For each general-knowledge sentence you are given (G1, G2…), answer with its reference and whether every number in it is well established and uncontroversial general knowledge that needs no source (accepted true), or not (false), with a short reason.

    F6: The Barrier Moisturiser comes in a 50 ml tube.
  P3: Mineral Sun Cream SPF 30 (Sun cream)
    F7: The Mineral Sun Cream SPF 30 uses zinc oxide as its only UV filter.
    F8: The Mineral Sun Cream SPF 30 is fragrance free.

<article>
Title: A simple skincare routine for sensitive skin

A simple skincare routine for sensitive skin comes down to three steps: cleanse, moisturise and protect. Keeping things gentle and simple is the best way to look after skin that reacts easily, and choosing the right products can make all the difference.

## Why a simple routine matters

Sensitive skin needs a little extra care. Everyone's skin is different, and what works for one person may not work for another. That is why it is so important to listen to your skin and give it what it needs. A simple routine is easier to stick to, and when it comes to skincare, consistency is key. Less really can be more.

## Step one: cleanse

Cleansing is an important part of any routine. It helps to remove the dirt and build-up of the day and leaves your skin feeling fresh. For sensitive skin, a gentle cleanser is a good choice. Our [Gentle Cream Cleanser](P1) is fragrance free [F1]. It has a pH of 5.5 [F2]. It comes in a 150 ml pump bottle [F3]. Cleansing gently and regularly can help your skin look and feel its best.

{{P1}}

## Step two: moisturise

Moisturising is another key step. Skin needs moisture to stay comfortable, and a good moisturiser can help it feel soft and cared for. It is worth choosing something that suits your skin. The [Barrier Moisturiser](P2) contains ceramides and niacinamide [F4]. It is fragrance free [F5]. It comes in a 50 ml tube [F6]. Moisturising every day is a simple habit that can make a real difference over time.

{{P2}}

## Step three: protect

Protecting your skin is just as important as cleansing and moisturising. Sun protection is something everyone should think about, all year round. The [Mineral Sun Cream SPF 30](P3) uses zinc oxide as its only UV filter [F7]. It is fragrance free [F8]. Making protection part of your routine is one of the best things you can do for your skin.

{{P3}}

## Finding what works for you

Building a routine takes time, and it is fine to go slowly. Pay attention to how your skin feels and make changes when you need to. Be patient, be gentle and be kind to your skin. With the right care, sensitive skin can feel calm and comfortable, and looking after it can become something you enjoy rather than a chore. Every small step counts. Browse our full [sensitive skin range](L1) to find the products that feel right for you.

</article>

<general_knowledge>
—
</general_knowledge>
